name: PASS_DEFINITIONS
description: The ordered set of named execution passes that structure the agent's work.
examples: Pass 1 — analysis: identify root cause; Pass 2 — implementation: minimal patch; Pass 3 — verification: run tests; Pass 4 — review: double-check assumptions
analysis → tdd → fix → verification → review
resolution: List the named passes in execution order, each with a one-line description of what the agent should do in that pass.
expected_format: an ordered list of pass names and their one-line description, separated by semicolons

name: CONTEXT_TARGET
description: The concrete codebase area, subsystem, file set, or runtime context that frames the task.
examples: the request router in internal/http
the flaky integration test around user sync
resolution: Fill this with the most specific target you can infer from the user request and current repository context.
expected_format: a short noun phrase naming the exact files, subsystem, runtime path, or failing surface being changed

name: DONE_CONDITION
description: The explicit stopping condition for the work loop.
examples: all targeted tests pass and the failing nil-path is covered
the compiler builds, the new contract test passes, and no unrelated files changed
resolution: State a concrete, verifiable definition of done tied to tests, build success, or the requested deliverable.
expected_format: one sentence with observable exit criteria and at least one verification signal

name: SCOPE_ELEMENTS
description: The code, behavior, files, or interfaces that must not be changed while solving the task.
examples: unrelated packages, generated files, and public CLI flags
the stable compiler pipeline outside the bugfix path
resolution: List the boundaries the agent must preserve based on the request, repository rules, and stable interfaces.
expected_format: a comma-separated list of files, behaviors, interfaces, or subsystems that must stay unchanged

name: STABLE_INTERFACE
description: The API, contract, output shape, or workflow that must remain stable after the change.
examples: the optimize JSON response fields consumed by agents
the existing categories and optimize command flags
resolution: Name the interface or contract reviewers should verify did not drift while implementing the task.
expected_format: one sentence naming the contract, API, output shape, or workflow that must not drift

name: TASK
description: The primary task statement the agent should solve.
examples: Fix the nil dereference in the optimizer and prove the fix with tests.
Add agent-facing docs for vokuprompt without changing core selection logic.
resolution: Restate the user's request as a precise execution goal, preserving constraints and success criteria.
expected_format: one imperative sentence starting with a verb and ending with the concrete deliverable or fix

name: UNIT
description: The smallest useful work unit the agent should iterate over.
examples: one failing test, then the minimal patch, then validation
one contract file or one CLI behavior at a time
resolution: Choose a deterministic work unit that keeps the task incremental and easy to validate.
expected_format: a short phrase describing one deterministic work chunk that can be completed and checked before moving on

name: VALIDATION
description: The exact verification command or proof the agent must run and report.
examples: go test ./... -v
npm test -- optimize-contract
resolution: Provide the real build, test, or lint command that proves the change worked in the current repository.
expected_format: a runnable shell command or short command chain copied exactly as it should be executed

name: OUTPUT_FORMAT
description: The exact structure or delivery shape the refined brief or final result should use.
examples: markdown with sections for Goal, Constraints, Validation, and Deliverables
JSON with fields for summary, risks, assumptions, and next_steps
resolution: State the concrete output structure the agent should produce so the rewritten brief is directly executable and reviewable.
expected_format: one short sentence or noun phrase naming the required output shape

name: AUDIENCE
description: The person or system the refined brief is primarily written for.
examples: a coding agent working inside this repository
a reviewer who must validate the resulting change
resolution: Name the real audience so the rewritten brief can use the right level of detail, constraints, and terminology.
expected_format: a short noun phrase naming the target reader, executor, or consumer

name: QUALITY_CRITERIA
description: The concrete standards that define whether the refined brief or resulting work is good enough.
examples: minimal patch, explicit validation, and no unrelated behavior changes
reviewable output, grounded assumptions, and runnable verification
resolution: List the specific quality bar the refined brief must make explicit so success is measurable rather than implied.
expected_format: a short comma-separated list of concrete standards or acceptance criteria

name: MISSING_INPUTS
description: The unresolved questions or facts that must be surfaced before the brief can be executed safely.
examples: the exact file or subsystem to change, required validation command, and whether docs must be updated
the target branch behavior, external constraints, and the expected output format
resolution: List the missing inputs that must be asked, inferred safely, or labeled as unresolved so the refined brief does not hide uncertainty.
expected_format: a short comma-separated list of unresolved questions, facts, or decisions

name: ASSUMPTIONS
description: The assumptions the agent may need to operate under until they are confirmed or replaced with facts.
examples: assume the change should stay within JSON registries unless code changes become necessary
assume the current Go test suite is the primary validation path unless the repo specifies more
resolution: State any provisional assumptions explicitly and label them clearly so reviewers can challenge them instead of inheriting hidden guesses.
expected_format: a short comma-separated list of provisional assumptions, each phrased plainly

name: CODE_AREA
description: The concrete subsystem, code path, or file cluster whose new understanding should be captured durably.
examples: the optimizer selection path in internal/engine
the CLI asset resolution flow in internal/cli
resolution: Fill this with the narrowest code area where meaningful new understanding emerged from the completed work.
expected_format: a short noun phrase naming the exact subsystem, runtime path, or file cluster that produced the learning

name: FILES_TOUCHED
description: The files changed or materially inspected while producing the learning that is being written back.
examples: internal/cli/optimize.go, internal/cli/optimize_test.go
categories.json, patterns.json, placeholders.json
resolution: List the concrete files that produced or now embody the durable learning, keeping the list tight and reviewable.
expected_format: a comma-separated list of repository-relative file paths

name: DISCOVERY_SCOPE
description: The investigation boundary or question that the discovery or memory write-back answers.
examples: how pattern role limits shape optimize output
why the flaky cache invalidation path fails under retries
resolution: State the exact discovery scope that was investigated so the memory stays bounded to the real question answered.
expected_format: one sentence or noun phrase naming the specific discovery question, boundary, or investigation target

name: LEARNING_TYPE
description: The kind of durable learning that emerged from the work.
examples: code discovery
implementation learning
resolution: Choose the most accurate learning type for the write-back, matching the memory-oriented category being executed.
expected_format: a short lower-case phrase naming the learning type or memory category

name: EVIDENCE_PATHS
description: The specific files, commands, logs, or tests that justify the memory being written.
examples: internal/engine/selection.go and go test ./... -v output
README.md, skills/vokuprompt/SKILL.md, and the compiled prompt contract tests
resolution: List the concrete evidence sources that support the claimed learning before any memory is updated.
expected_format: a concise list of repository paths, commands, or logs that directly justify the memory content

name: PRIOR_ASSUMPTION
description: The earlier belief, claim, or working assumption that existed before the new evidence was gathered.
examples: the optimizer could silently choose memory categories from intent alone
the failure was caused by network timing rather than stale cache state
resolution: Capture the prior assumption that is being reviewed, corrected, or preserved so the memory shows what changed.
expected_format: one sentence stating the prior belief, claim, or assumption in plain language

name: UPDATED_ASSUMPTION
description: The corrected or confirmed understanding after reviewing evidence.
examples: memory categories are explicit user- or agent-selected contracts, not auto-detected workflows
the retry bug comes from stale cache invalidation order, not network timing
resolution: State the updated understanding that should replace or refine the prior assumption in durable memory.
expected_format: one sentence stating the corrected or confirmed understanding

name: MEMORY_KIND
description: The type of repo-local memory entry that should be written or updated.
examples: debugging digest
architecture memory
resolution: Name the durable memory artifact being updated, aligned with the selected category and the kind of understanding captured.
expected_format: a short noun phrase naming the memory entry type

name: MEMORY_TARGET_FILE
description: The repo-local file where the durable memory should be written or updated.
examples: .copilot/memory/architecture.md
docs/agent-memory/debugging.md
resolution: Point to the existing repo-local memory file to update, or the agreed repo-local target file if a new durable note is warranted.
expected_format: one repository-relative file path for the repo-local memory store

name: CONFIDENCE_LEVEL
description: The confidence attached to the memory write-back based on the available evidence.
examples: high: validated by tests and direct code inspection
medium: code inspection complete, but runtime reproduction still pending
resolution: State a concise confidence level tied to the evidence quality and any remaining uncertainty.
expected_format: a short confidence label plus brief justification

name: OPEN_QUESTIONS
description: The unresolved questions or follow-ups that should remain explicitly open after the memory write-back.
examples: whether the same selection edge case exists in future category bundles
whether the flaky path can be reproduced under race-enabled CI
resolution: List only the unresolved questions that still matter after the new learning is saved, and keep them separate from verified facts.
expected_format: a short list or one sentence naming the remaining unknowns or follow-up questions

name: COVERAGE_THRESHOLD
description: The minimum percentage-point increase in test coverage that must be achieved.
examples: 10 percentage points
at least 8%
resolution: Use the percentage or point target from the user request, defaulting to 5% if none is specified.
expected_format: a short numeric string with a percent sign or the phrase 'percentage points' (e.g., '5%')

name: COVERAGE_SCOPE
description: The package, module, directory, or file set where coverage must be measured and improved.
examples: internal/engine
the parser package at internal/ast
all files under pkg/auth
resolution: Fill with the narrowest package or file cluster where coverage improvement is required.
expected_format: a short noun phrase naming the exact package path, directory, or file cluster

name: HANDOFF_SCOPE
description: The downstream audience, next-task boundary, or handoff scope that the memory should safely support.
examples: the next agent continuing optimize contract work
the maintainer reviewing the architecture note before the next refactor
resolution: Describe who or what future work this durable memory is meant to help so the write-back stays focused and safely scoped.
expected_format: one sentence or noun phrase naming the downstream user, next task, or handoff boundary
